note: PHASE 10 START -- slot 1 of the three left open when phase 9 closed its two named deliverables. DELIVERABLE: check:integrity now rejects raw C0 control bytes (and DEL) outside tab/LF/CR. The gap was measured, not theorised: check-image-widths.mjs shipped to main carrying a raw 0x08 at byte 9117, where the mount had eaten the backslash out of a word-boundary escape inside a comment that reads 'no escaped backslash literals'. Injecting the same byte into a copy and running the scanner reported 'ok (897 files checked, 0 issues)' -- the guard only ever looked for null bytes and truncation, so ANY C0 byte passed ANYWHERE in a file, not merely inside string literals as first reported. node --check and eslint both parse such files, so no layer below caught it either. The rule is a flat ban rather than an allowlist: an exemption for 'benign' control bytes would blind the guard to exactly the corruption class it exists to catch. Two pre-existing offenders found by the pre-flight sweep and FIXED in this ship rather than exempted, both the same mount bug and both still functionally correct by luck -- four raw ESC bytes in check-cancelled-occurrence-passthrough.mjs ANSI colour constants, and one in fetch-vercel-build-log.mjs inside an ANSI-strip REGEX LITERAL; replaced with proper x1b escapes and proven byte-identical in output.
